newsitem.title: JAPAN: BA hopes to boost Japan growth with new image.
newsitem.headline: BA hopes to boost Japan growth with new image.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday it hopes a planned facelift to its corporate image will help lure more Japanese customers to its flights.
British Airways on Tuesday unveiled a three-year expansion plan which will include new routes, new services and ethnic artwork painted on its aircraft.

Revenue on the airline's flights in and out of Japan is growing by 10 to 12 percent a year and the new corporate image is expected to help boost that further, BA's general manager for Japan, Chris Garton, told a news conference in Tokyo.
"The market is growing about 10, 11, 12 percent a year for us at the moment and we would hope to continue at that and more," Garton said.

"Japanese people are very keen on new images and new style, and innovative approach. We think it (the expansion plan) will add one more (factor) to our, what we believe is, already good image," he said.
In the year ending in March 1997, passenger revenue accounted for about 90 percent of British Airways' total revenue in Japan, with cargo accounting for the remaining 10 percent, Garton said.
The cost of redesigning and marketing the new corporate image was expected to be around $100 million, according to British Airways officials.
